goal.p1: This project was born out of the desire to determine the real percentage raise in salary, in relation to the loss of purchasing power due to inflation since the previous raise.
goal.p2: This tool only gives an idea. Every situation is unique and inflation applies differently. If you want to delve deeper into the subject of inflation, there are many more detailed and accurate sources.
goal.title: Goal

legal.p1: No data is collected at any point.
legal.title: Legal Notices

why.p1: In the course of 2022, inflation rates soared in France (and in Europe overall). Many wondered whether the annual "raises" would, at least, cover the rise in prices and the loss of purchasing power.
why.p2: Turns out the question was relevant for all previous years, but we don't often think about it.
why.title: About

inflation.title: Where do inflation rates come from?

operating.p1: The oldest salary is your reference income. This salary allows you to buy a {stuff}.
operating.p2: Over time, because of the inflation going on, the same {stuff} is going to be increasingly expensive. As a result, you salary will allow you to buy only a smaller portion of that same {stuff}.
operating.p3: Following raises are then recalculated to reflect how they allow you to buy the same {stuff}.
operating.p4: The change in the ability to buy the {stuff} is represented on the chart by the gap between the announced salary and the adjusted salary.
operating.title: How does it work?

p1.p: Over {link}, fill in the successive salary changes over time.

usage.p2: You will be able to see the percentage raise announced, and below, the real change adjusted with the inflation. You will also see the next required percentage raise to mitigate the loss of purchasing power since the last change of salary.

p3.p: Over {link}, you will be able to change the income calculation mode between annual gross income with imposition, and net monthly.

header.title: # Detailed report — Did I get a raise?
header.purpose: This report contains all the data used, the detailed month-by-month calculations and the sources of the inflation rates. It is meant to be shared, especially during a salary negotiation, and allows anyone to independently verify every result.

data.title: ## Data used
data.customNote: These rates are custom rates entered manually; they do not come from an official source.

calculations.title: ## Calculation details

formulaIncome.gross-annual: - Net monthly income = gross annual salary × (1 − taxation / 100) / 12
formulaIncome.hourly-rate: - Net monthly income = hourly rate × monthly hours × (1 − taxation / 100)

calculations.formulaMultiplier: - Cumulated inflation multiplier = ∏ (1 + monthly rate / 100), starting from the month after the reference salary
calculations.formulaAdjusted: - Adjusted salary = net monthly income / cumulated multiplier
calculations.formulaChange: - Real change (%) = (adjusted salary / previous adjusted salary − 1) × 100
calculations.minimalRaise: - Minimal raise required to compensate inflation: {raise}%

integrity.title: ## Data integrity
integrity.explanation: So that anyone can verify this report was not modified after its generation, the SHA-256 fingerprint of the JSON data block below is included here. Anyone can recompute this fingerprint from the JSON block: if the result matches, the data has not been tampered with.
integrity.howToVerify: To verify: `echo -n <JSON block> | sha256sum` (or using any online SHA-256 calculator). The result must match the fingerprint above.
integrity.selfHash: 1. Recompute the SHA-256 fingerprint of the JSON block from the “Data integrity” section. 2. Compare it with the fingerprint given in that same section. 3. Redo the calculations with the documented formulas: any difference reveals an alteration. Fingerprint:
